(1) Like-charge colloidal interactions can be strongly attractive in a confined geometry; (2) This attraction is suppressed by a conducting bounding surface, and (3) It is suppressed by the presence of a small amount of salt in solution.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
like-charged colloids confined to a thin layer between charged glass plates exhibit long-ranged attraction at high ionic strength and short-ranged repulsion at low ionic strength.

The main takeaway from our work is that
electrostatic interactions in confined colloidal suspensions are not always well described by the standard DLVO theory.
the electrostatic interactions between colloidal particles in a thin layer can be significantly modified by the presence of conducting bounding surfaces.
the presence of a conducting wall, even at large distances, can significantly modify the interactions between colloidal particles in the bulk of a solution.
